questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 26 days. A alone can complete it in 52 days. If B works at 50 percent efficiency, then in how many days A and B together will complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

A completes the work in 52 days.

A and B together complete the work in 26 days.

B works at 50% efficiency.

Formula/Concept:

Efficiency = Work completed / Time taken

Solution Steps:

A completes work in 52 days, so A's efficiency is 1/52 per day.

B works at 50% efficiency of A,

⇒ B's efficiency is 1/2 × 1/52 = 1/104 per day.

When A and B work together, their combined efficiency is

⇒ 1/52 + 1/104 = 3/104 per day.

Let D be the number of days required for A and B to complete the work. 

We can set up the equation: 3/104 × D = W.

Simplifying the equation, we have D = 104 / 3.

**Therefore, A and B together will complete the work in 104/3 days.**

Time taken by B to finish the work = 13 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

**Calculation:**

Ratio of efficiency of A and B = 130 : 100

⇒ 13 : 10

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

⇒ Ratio of time taken by A and B = 10 : 13

Let A takes x days to do the same job

⇒ 10 : 13 : : x : 13

⇒ 10/13 : : x/13

⇒ x = (10/13 × 13)

⇒ x = 10 days

**∴ The time taken by A to finish the job is 10 days**

Total Work & Efficiency Trick

Total work is universally taken as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of individual completion times. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Alternate Days Working

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 persons) and scale it up to reach the closest multiple near the total work.

Work & Wages Distribution

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total units of work completed by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are directly distributed based on their efficiencies.

questions.question: John can do a work in 12 days and Anju in 20 days. If they work on it together for 6 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:

Combined efficiency = (60 ÷ 12) + (60 ÷ 20) = 5 + 3 = 8 units/day

This concept operates identically to Time and Work. The primary difference is that a leakage or outlet pipe is assigned a negative efficiency because it empties the tank.

When multiple people work together, total wages are distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If they work for the exact same number of days, the wages can be directly divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

If two individuals work on alternating days, calculate the total work completed in a 2-day cycle first. Then, multiply this cycle to get closest to the total work, followed by adding the remaining work for the person whose turn is next.

questions.solution:
P alone can do a work in 25 days

Part of work done by P in a day = 1/25

questions.question: P and Q together can do a job in 15 days. P is thrice as efficient as Q. In how many days can P alone do the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P and Q can do a job in 15 days, P is 3 times as efficient as Q.

**Concept:**

Work done is directly proportional to efficiency.

**Solution:**

If Q's efficiency is q, then P's efficiency is 3q.

(P + Q)'s 1 day's work = (3q + q) = 4q = 1/15

Then, q = 1/60.

P's 1 day's work = 3q = 3/60 = 1/20.

**Therefore, P can complete the job alone in 20 days.**

questions.question: A and B working separately can mow a field in 12 and 10 hours, respectively. They work alternately, each for 1 hour, beginning with A, at 5:00 a.m. At what time will the mowing be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can mow the field in 12 hours, so A's work rate = 1/12 of the field per hour.

B can mow the field in 10 hours, so B's work rate = 1/10 of the field per hour.

They work alternately, starting with A at 5:00 a.m.

**Formula used:**

Total work completed in 2 hours = Work done by A + Work done by B.

Remaining work = Total work - Work done.

**Calculations:**

Work done by A in 1 hour = 1/12.

Work done by B in 1 hour = 1/10.

Total work completed in 2 hours = (1/12) + (1/10) = (5 + 6)/60 = 11/60.

Total time taken:

In 2 hours, they complete 11/60 of the work.

Work remaining after 5 full cycles (10 hours):

Total work done in 10 hours = (11/60) × 5 = 55/60.

Remaining work = 1 - 55/60 = 5/60 = 1/12.

At 5:00 a.m., A starts again for the last 1/12 of the work.

Time taken by A to finish 1/12 = 1 hour.

**Final time:**

10 hours of work + 1 hour (A finishes the remaining work) = 11 hours.

Start time = 5:00 a.m.

End time = 5:00 a.m. + 11 hours = 4:00 p.m.

**∴ The mowing will be completed at 4:00 p.m.**

questions.question: A, B and C alone can do a work in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. All three of them began the work together but B left 3 days before completion of the work. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 10 days.

B can complete the work in 12 days.

C can complete the work in 15 days.

B left 3 days before the completion of the work.

**Formula used:**

Work done per day by A = 1/10

Work done per day by B = 1/12

Work done per day by C = 1/15

**Calculation:**

Let the total time taken to complete the work be X days.

B worked for (X - 3) days.

Total work done by A in X days = X × (1/10)

Total work done by B in (X - 3) days = (X - 3) × (1/12)

Total work done by C in X days = X × (1/15)

The total work completed is 1, so:

⇒ X/10 + (X - 3)/12 + X/15 = 1

Taking LCM of 10, 12, and 15:

⇒ (6X + 5(X - 3) + 4X) / 60 = 1

⇒ (6X + 5X - 15 + 4X) / 60 = 1

⇒ (15X - 15) / 60 = 1

⇒ 15X - 15 = 60

⇒ 15X = 75

⇒ X = 5

**Therefore, the work was completed in 5 days.**

questions.question: Mohi and Suniti working separately can do a work in 12 and 15 days, respectively. Mohi starts the work and they work on alternate days. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mohi can finish work in 12 days

Suniti can finish work in 15 days

For work done on alternate days, we first find the total work by taking the LCM of the two individual days. The total work done in 2 days is the sum of their individual work.

**Solution:**

⇒ Total work = LCM of 12 and 15 = 60 units

⇒ Work done by Mohi in a day = (60)/(12) = 5 units

⇒ Work done by Suniti in a day = (60)/(15) = 4 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days = 5 + 4 = 9 units

So 12 days of work will be 9 × 54 units.

13th day mohi will work = 54 + 5 = 59.

Now 1 unit is done by Suniti in 1/4 days.

⇒ Time taken to complete the work = 13(1)/(4) days

**Hence, the work will be completed in 13(1)/(4) days.**

questions.question: Amrit is thrice as good a workman as Bhagat. Therefore Amrit is able to finish a piece of work in 50 days less than Bhagat. The time (in days) in which they can finish it working together is:
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Work rate of Amrit = 3 × Work rate of Bhagat,

Time difference = 50 days 

**Concept:**

The work rate is inversely proportional to the time taken.

The work rate of (Amrit + Bhagat) = Work rate of Amrit + Work rate of Bhagat

**Solution:**

⇒ Time taken by Bhagat (B) = Time taken by Amrit (A) + 50

⇒ But A = B/3 because Amrit is thrice as good a workman as Bhagat

⇒ Substituting, we get B = B/3 + 50

⇒ Solving, B = 75 days and A = 25 days

⇒ Working together, they can finish the work in 1/(1/A + 1/B) = 1/(1/25 + 1/75) = 18.75 days = 18(3)/(4) days

**Therefore, they can finish the work in **18(3)/(4)** days working together.**

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a work in 30 days, 15 days and 20 days respectively. P works on first day, then Q works on second day and then R works on third day and so on. In how many days the work will be Completed?

So, total work completed in 3 days = (2 + 4 + 3) = 9 units

We can take this 3 days work as 1 cycle

∴ in 6 cycles work completed = 9 × 6 = 54 units

Remaining work = 60 units – 54 units = 6 units

(1 cycle = 3 days)

∴ 6 cycles = 6 × 3 = 18 days

19th day P come on work

Work done by P on 19th day = 2 units

Work left after 19 days = 60 – 56 = 4 units

Q work on 20th day

Q complete the remaining work on 20th day

**Total time taken to complete the work = 20days**

questions.question: A1 alone can do a work in 12 days and A2 alone can do the same work in 15 days. With help of A3, they finish the same work in 5 days. In how many days A3 alone can do the same work ?

**Formula:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(12, 15, 5) = 60 units

Time taken by A3 to complete the work = 60/3 = 20 days

questions.question: If A can do a piece of work in 16 days and B can do the same work in 24 days, the least whole number of days to complete the work, if they start working on alternate days, is:

Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the time taken is used to calculate work capacity per day.

Total work = 48 units (assume the total work is 48 units for simplicity).

Work done by A in 1 day = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units.

Work done by B in 1 day = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 units.

In 2 days, A and B together complete:

Work = 3 + 2 = 5 units.

Number of complete 2-day cycles = 48 ÷ 5 = 9 cycles (9 × 5 = 45 units).

Remaining work = 48 - 45 = 3 units.

On the 19th day, A works (as it is A's turn):

A completes 3 units in 1 day.

**∴ The least whole number of days to complete the work is 19 days.**

questions.question: A and B can together finish a work in 30 days. They worked together for 20 days and then B left. After another 20 days, A finished the remaining work. In how many days can A alone finish the whole work?

Worked together for 20 days, then B left

A worked for another 20 days

**Concept: **

If A and B together finish work in 'a' days, A finishes alone in 'b' days and B finishes alone in 'c' days, then 1/a = 1/b + 1/c.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work done by A and B in 20 days = 20/30 = 2/3 of the work

⇒ Work done by A in the next 20 days = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the work

⇒ Therefore, A alone can finish the work in 20 × 3 = 60 days.

**Hence, A alone can finish the whole work in 60 days.**

questions.question: If 108 workers can build a wall in 36 days, then in how many days can 48 workers build the same wall?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

108 workers can build a wall in 36 days.

We need to find how many days 48 workers will take to build the same wall.

**Formula Used:**

Number of workers × Number of days = Constant work

**Calculation:**

Let the number of days required for 48 workers to build the wall be x .

According to the formula:

108 workers × 36 days = 48 workers × x days

⇒ 108 × 36 = 48 × x

⇒ x = (108 × 36) / 48

⇒ x = 3888 / 48

⇒ x = 81

**The number of days 48 workers will take to build the same wall is 81 days.**
